key_insight: The paper shows that neural operators can be built directly from numerical discretizations, suggesting they may learn the underlying finite element/finite difference scheme rather than an abstract PDE operator alone.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more interpretable and parameter-efficient path to surrogate models for PDE-based solid mechanics and other FEM-driven simulations.
method: Constructs neural operator basis functions using finite element concepts, either by approximating or directly learning the basis with neural networks.
Unrolls finite-difference time stepping into iterative neural architectures that produce basis coefficients.
Uses numerical analysis to derive convergence/error bounds for these discretization-inspired operator networks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing reduced errors and improved parameter efficiency, alongside theoretical convergence estimates with polynomial network-size dependence on L2 accuracy.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the chosen discretization and PDE class, so the approach may not transfer equally well to all operator-learning settings or mesh types.
paper_title: Numerical Neural Operator: Connection Between Numerical Analysis and the Operator Learning and Building Discretized Neural Operators from Finite Element Methods
